result:
I tested 7 claims about `setuptools.package_index` and found 2 real bugs. One is serious: a URL can make `download()` write a file anywhere the user can write.

**Bug 1: download path escapes `tmpdir` (High)**
- **What happens:** `_resolve_download_filename` decodes `%2F` in the last part of the URL into `/`. When the decoded name is an absolute path, `os.path.join(tmpdir, name)` ignores `tmpdir`. The code already strips `..`, but it never checks for an absolute name.
- **Why it's a bug:** The `download` docstring promises the file goes "to a subpath of `tmpdir`".
- **Proof:** I ran an end-to-end check with the network call replaced by a stub. `download("https://example.com/pkg/%2Ftmp%2Fpi_e2e%2Fescaped.tar.gz", "/tmp/pi_e2e/tmpdir")` wrote `/tmp/pi_e2e/escaped.tar.gz` and left `tmpdir` empty. Hypothesis found the smallest case: `https://example.com/d/%2F` resolves to `/`.
- **Context:** Download URLs come from remote index pages, so an attacker can control them. This is CVE-2025-47273, the vulnerability this checkout is named after.
- **Fix:** The report includes a patch that raises `ValueError` when the joined path doesn't start with `tmpdir`. I didn't run that patch against the test.

**Bug 2: `find_external_links` slows down quadratically (Medium)**
- **What happens:** In the `REL` regex, `[^>]*` also matches `<`. On a page full of `"< "` with no `>`, each `<` scans to the end of the page, so time grows with the square of the page size: 16 KB took 0.5 s, 32 KB took 2.05 s and 64 KB took 8.2 s.
- **Why it matters:** The function scans every fetched index page, which is untrusted HTML, so a hostile page can hang the client. This regex was introduced to fix an earlier slowdown bug of the same kind (CVE-2022-40897), and it is still quadratic.
- **Fix:** Changing the class to `[^<>]*` brings the 64 KB case from 8.3 s to 0.001 s. It gave the same matches as the old regex on the 4 well-formed sample tags I tried.

**Passed:** 4 tests, covering `_encode_auth` (decodes back to the original), `htmldecode` (matches `html.unescape`), `_splituser` and `parse_bdist_wininst`. I confirmed only one of these could fail: `htmldecode` agrees with `html.unescape` even on `&amp` without a semicolon. I didn't build failing inputs for the other three. `_vcs_split_rev_from_url` is listed as CLAIM-7 in `claims.md`, but I didn't write a test for it.

One change to the claims: I first required the download path to be strictly inside `tmpdir`. The URL `.../d/.` resolves to `tmpdir` itself, which does no harm (the write just fails), so I relaxed the test to check only for escapes and noted the change in `claims.md`.

Files are in `runs/setuptools-pkgindex_v2_r1/`:
- `claims.md`
- `test_package_index.py`
- `bug_report_setuptools_package_index_PackageIndex_download_2026-10-28_18-04_dk0g.md`
- `bug_report_setuptools_package_index_find_external_links_2026-10-28_18-04_3nbc.md`
